│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via crafted PHP file in
│                        │       │                    omni-completion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0736, the PHP omni-completion script in
│                        │       │                   runtime/autoload/phpcomplete.vim interpolates a class or
│                        │       │                   trait name, taken from the contents of the edited buffer,
│                        │       │                   into a search() pattern that is run via win_execute()
│                        │       │                   without escaping. A name containing a single quote can
│                        │       │                   terminate the search() string argument early, and because
│                        │       │                   the bar is honored as an Ex command separator, the
│                        │       │                   remainder of the name is run as Ex commands; via the :!
│                        │       │                   command this allows arbitrary operating-system command
│                        │       │                   execution when a victim opens a crafted PHP file and
│                        │       │                   invokes omni-completion. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0736.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary command execution via crafted tags
│                        │       │                   file in C omni-completion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0735, the C omni-completion script in
│                        │       │                   runtime/autoload/ccomplete.vim interpolates the typeref:
│                        │       │                   or typename: extension field of a tags entry, without
│                        │       │                   escaping, into a :vimgrep pattern that is run through
│                        │       │                   :execute. Because :vimgrep honors the bar as a command
│                        │       │                   separator, a crafted tag field can close the search
│                        │       │                   pattern and append an arbitrary Ex command; opening a
│                        │       │                   hostile .c file whose project tags file contains such an
│                        │       │                   entry and invoking C omni-completion runs that command as
│                        │       │                   the editing user. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0735.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow allows arbitrary code
│                        │       │                   execution 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0846, set_sofo() in src/spellfile.c reuses
│                        │       │                   sl_sal_first[] without resetting values left by
│                        │       │                   set_sal_first(), so a crafted spell file containing an
│                        │       │                   SN_SAL section before an SN_SOFO section causes
│                        │       │                   under-counted mapping lists and attacker-influenced writes
│                        │       │                    beyond a heap allocation. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0846.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary command execution via crafted tags
│                        │       │                   file in C omni-completion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0845, StructMembers() in
│                        │       │                   runtime/autoload/ccomplete.vim constructs and executes a
│                        │       │                   vimgrep command using an insufficiently escaped typeref:
│                        │       │                   or typename: value from a tags file, allowing an
│                        │       │                   unterminated collection followed by a command separator to
│                        │       │                    execute arbitrary Ex and operating-system commands when a
│                        │       │                    user invokes C omni-completion with CTRL-X CTRL-O on a
│                        │       │                   member access whose type is resolved from that tags file.
│                        │       │                   This issue is fixed in version 9.2.0845.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary command execution via crafted vimball 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0847, runtime/autoload/vimball.vim allows a crafted
│                        │       │                   vimball member named .VimballRecord to overwrite the
│                        │       │                   installation record with attacker-chosen commands. When
│                        │       │                   vimball#RmVimball() later processes the matching record
│                        │       │                   entry, the stored Ex commands, including operating-system
│                        │       │                   commands invoked through :!, execute with the privileges
│                        │       │                   of the user running Vim. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0847.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary Code Execution via Insecure Shell
│                        │       │                   Command Handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0839, the runtime/ftplugin/sh.vim,
│                        │       │                   runtime/ftplugin/zsh.vim, and runtime/ftplugin/ps1.vim
│                        │       │                   filetype plugins pass attacker-controlled Visual-mode
│                        │       │                   selections from K through keywordprg commands without
│                        │       │                   safely separating shell arguments. fnameescape() and
│                        │       │                   PATH_ESC_CHARS do not neutralize shell metacharacters
│                        │       │                   before ShKeywordPrg, ZshKeywordPrg, or GetHelp invokes
│                        │       │                   bash, zsh, or PowerShell, allowing arbitrary
│                        │       │                   operating-system commands to execute with the privileges
│                        │       │                   of the user running Vim. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0839.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary Code Execution via Crafted Netrw Menu
│                        │       │                   Entries 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0840, runtime/plugin/netrwPlugin.vim loads netrw and
│                        │       │                   runtime/pack/dist/opt/netrw/autoload/netrw.vim constructs
│                        │       │                   Bookmarks, History, and Targets menu entries by
│                        │       │                   interpolating attacker-controlled directory paths into
│                        │       │                   executed :menu commands. s:NetrwBookmarkMenu(),
│                        │       │                   s:NetrwTgtMenu(), g:netrw_menu_escape, EX_TRLBAR, and
│                        │       │                   netrw#MakeTgt() fail to neutralize the | command separator
│                        │       │                    or single quotes at five construction sites, allowing a
│                        │       │                   crafted path browsed or bookmarked in GUI Vim to execute
│                        │       │                   arbitrary Ex and operating-system commands. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0840. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : HIGH

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim path traversial 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.1.1552, a path traversal issue in Vim’s tar.vim
│                        │       │                   plugin can allow overwriting of arbitrary files when
│                        │       │                   opening specially crafted tar archives. Impact is low
│                        │       │                   because this exploit requires direct user interaction.
│                        │       │                   However, successfully exploitation can lead to overwriting
│                        │       │                    sensitive files or placing executable code in privileged
│                        │       │                   locations, depending on the permissions of the process
│                        │       │                   editing the archive. The victim must edit such a file
│                        │       │                   using Vim which will reveal the filename and the file
│                        │       │                   content, a careful user may suspect some strange things
│                        │       │                   going on. Successful exploitation could results in the
│                        │       │                   ability to execute arbitrary commands on the underlying
│                        │       │                   operating system. Version 9.1.1552 contains a patch for
│                        │       │                   the vulnerability.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via 'helpfile' option
│                        │       │                   processing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.1.2132, a heap buffer overflow vulnerability
│                        │       │                   exists in Vim's tag file resolution logic when processing
│                        │       │                   the 'helpfile' option. The vulnerability is located in the
│                        │       │                    get_tagfname() function in src/tag.c. When processing
│                        │       │                   help file tags, Vim copies the user-controlled 'helpfile'
│                        │       │                   option value into a fixed-size heap buffer of MAXPATHL + 1
│                        │       │                    bytes (typically 4097 bytes) using an unsafe STRCPY()
│                        │       │                   operation without any bounds checking. This issue has been
│                        │       │                    patched in version 9.1.2132. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Information disclosure via heap-based buffer
│                        │       │                   overflow in Emacs-style tags file parsing 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0074, a heap-based buffer overflow
│                        │       │                   out-of-bounds read exists in Vim's Emacs-style tags file
│                        │       │                   parsing logic. When processing a malformed tags file, Vim
│                        │       │                   can be tricked into reading up to 7 bytes beyond the
│                        │       │                   allocated memory boundary. Version 9.2.0074 fixes the
│                        │       │                   issue.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Command injection allows arbitrary code execution via
│                        │       │                    malicious tag files 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0357, A command injection vulnerability exists in
│                        │       │                   Vim's tag file processing. When resolving a tag, the
│                        │       │                   filename field from the tags file is passed through
│                        │       │                   wildcard expansion to resolve environment variables and
│                        │       │                   wildcards. If the filename field contains backtick syntax
│                        │       │                   (e.g., `command`), Vim executes the embedded command via
│                        │       │                   the system shell with the full privileges of the running
│                        │       │                   user.

│                        │       ├ Title           : Vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via OS command
│                        │       │                   injection in netrw plugin 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0383, an OS command injection vulnerability
│                        │       │                   exists in the netrw standard plugin bundled with Vim. By
│                        │       │                   inducing a user to open a crafted URL (e.g., using the
│                        │       │                   sftp:// or file:// protocol handlers), an attacker can
│                        │       │                   execute arbitrary shell commands with the privileges of
│                        │       │                   the Vim process. This issue has been patched in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0383.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary command execution via :find
│                        │       │                   command-line completion 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0435, an OS command injection vulnerability
│                        │       │                   exists in Vim's :find command-line completion. When the
│                        │       │                   path option contains backtick-enclosed shell commands,
│                        │       │                   those commands are executed during file name completion.
│                        │       │                   Because the path option lacks the P_SECURE flag, it can be
│                        │       │                    set from a modeline, allowing an attacker who controls
│                        │       │                   the contents of a file to execute arbitrary shell commands
│                        │       │                    when the user opens that file in Vim and triggers :find
│                        │       │                   completion. This issue has been patched in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0435.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow allows arbitrary code
│                        │       │                   execution or denial of service 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0450, a heap buffer overflow exists in
│                        │       │                   read_compound() in src/spellfile.c when loading a crafted
│                        │       │                   spell file (.spl) with UTF-8 encoding active. An
│                        │       │                   attacker-controlled length field in the spell file's
│                        │       │                   compound section overflows a 32-bit signed integer
│                        │       │                   multiplication, causing a small buffer to be allocated for
│                        │       │                    a write loop that runs many iterations, overflowing the
│                        │       │                   heap. Because the 'spelllang' option can be set from a
│                        │       │                   modeline, a text file modeline can trigger spell file
│                        │       │                   loading if a malicious .spl file has been planted on the
│                        │       │                   runtimepath. This issue has been patched in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0450.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Arbitrary code execution via crafted
│                        │       │                   step-definition patterns 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0496, a code injection vulnerability exists in
│                        │       │                    s:stepmatch() in the cucumber filetype plugin
│                        │       │                   (runtime/ftplugin/cucumber.vim) on Vim builds with +ruby
│                        │       │                   support. Step-definition patterns read from .rb files
│                        │       │                   under the repository's features/*/ or stories/*/
│                        │       │                   directories are embedded into a Ruby Kernel.eval argument
│                        │       │                   without sufficient escaping, allowing a crafted pattern in
│                        │       │                    an attacker-controlled repository to execute arbitrary
│                        │       │                   Ruby (and through it arbitrary shell commands) when the
│                        │       │                   user invokes a step-jump mapping ([d, ]d). This issue has
│                        │       │                   been patched in version 9.2.0496.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Denial of Service via crafted spell file 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0662, the dump_prefixes() function in src/spell.c
│                        │       │                   walks a spell-file prefix trie iteratively with a depth
│                        │       │                   counter while dumping the prefixes that apply to a word.
│                        │       │                   The counter is bounded only by the trie structure itself;
│                        │       │                   it is never checked against the size of the fixed
│                        │       │                   MAXWLEN-element stack arrays it indexes (prefix[],
│                        │       │                   arridx[], curi[]). A crafted .spl file, loaded when the
│                        │       │                   user dumps the word list, can drive the descent
│                        │       │                   arbitrarily deep, so the function writes past the end of
│                        │       │                   those arrays. This is a stack out-of-bounds write that
│                        │       │                   corrupts the call frame and crashes the editor. This
│                        │       │                   vulnerability is fixed in 9.2.0662. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Out-of-bounds Read with libsodium-encrypted Files 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0671, when Vim opens a file encrypted with the
│                        │       │                   VimCrypt~04! or VimCrypt~05!
│                        │       │                   method (xchacha20poly1305, requires the +sodium feature)
│                        │       │                   whose body is shorter than a single libsodium secretstream
│                        │       │                    header, an unsigned length calculation underflows and a
│                        │       │                   subsequent decryption call reads far past the end of the
│                        │       │                   input buffer, crashing Vim. This vulnerability is fixed in
│                        │       │                    9.2.0671.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds write in
│                        │       │                   spell sound-folding 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0725, the single-byte branch of spell_soundfold_sal()
│                        │       │                   in src/spell.c translates a word through a spell file's
│                        │       │                   SAL sound-folding rules into a caller-owned result buffer,
│                        │       │                    but its result writes are guarded with reslen < MAXWLEN,
│                        │       │                   allowing reslen to reach MAXWLEN before res[reslen] = NUL
│                        │       │                   writes one byte past the end of the MAXWLEN-element stack
│                        │       │                   buffer. A boundary-length word passed to soundfold(), or
│                        │       │                   reached via sound-based spell suggestion while a SAL-based
│                        │       │                    spell language is active under a non-multibyte 8-bit
│                        │       │                   encoding, can corrupt the eval_soundfold() stack frame and
│                        │       │                    crash the editor. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │       │                   9.2.0725. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Stack Buffer Overflow via unbounded socket
│                        │       │                   connections 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0842, the socket server backend in src/socketserver.c
│                        │       │                   accepts unbounded client connections in
│                        │       │                   socketserver_accept(), causing descriptors to overflow
│                        │       │                   fd_set structures in src/channel.c and fixed-size struct
│                        │       │                   pollfd arrays in src/os_unix.c, which allows a local
│                        │       │                   process that can connect to the server socket to corrupt
│                        │       │                   stack memory or terminate the Vim server. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0842.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Heap buffer overflow via integer wraparound in
│                        │       │                   text property handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   9.2.0841, prop_add_one() in src/textprop.c uses the
│                        │       │                   proplen value from get_text_props() to increment a
│                        │       │                   uint16_t property count beyond 0xffff, wrapping the count
│                        │       │                   to zero and copying existing text-property records into a
│                        │       │                   heap allocation sized for none of them. This issue is
│                        │       │                   fixed in version 9.2.0841.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: netrw plugin: FTP username and password disclosure 
│                        │       ├ Description     : autoload/netrw.vim (aka the Netrw Plugin) 109, 131, and
│                        │       │                   other versions before 133k for Vim 7.1.266, other 7.1
│                        │       │                   versions, and 7.2 stores credentials for an FTP session,
│                        │       │                   and sends those credentials when attempting to establish
│                        │       │                   subsequent FTP sessions to servers on different hosts,
│                        │       │                   which allows remote FTP servers to obtain sensitive
│                        │       │                   information in opportunistic circumstances by logging
│                        │       │                   usernames and passwords.  NOTE: the upstream vendor
│                        │       │                   disputes a vector involving different ports on the same
│                        │       │                   host, stating "I'm assuming that they're using the same id
│                        │       │                    and password on that unchanged hostname, deliberately."[

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Information disclosure and denial of service via
│                        │       │                    malformed tags file 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0075, a heap-based buffer underflow exists in
│                        │       │                   Vim's Emacs-style tags file parsing logic. When processing
│                        │       │                    a malformed tags file where a delimiter appears at the
│                        │       │                   start of a line, Vim attempts to read memory immediately
│                        │       │                   preceding the allocated buffer. Version 9.2.0075 fixes the
│                        │       │                    issue.

│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: NFA regex engine NULL pointer dereference 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. From
│                        │       │                   9.1.0011 to before 9.2.0137, Vim's NFA regex compiler,
│                        │       │                   when encountering a collection containing a combining
│                        │       │                   character as the endpoint of a character range (e.g.
│                        │       │                   [0-0\u05bb]), incorrectly emits the composing bytes of
│                        │       │                   that character as separate NFA states. This corrupts the
│                        │       │                   NFA postfix stack, resulting in NFA_START_COLL having a
│                        │       │                   NULL out1 pointer. When nfa_max_width() subsequently
│                        │       │                   traverses the compiled NFA to estimate match width for the
│                        │       │                    look-behind assertion, it dereferences state->out1->out
│                        │       │                   without a NULL check, causing a segmentation fault. This
│                        │       │                   vulnerability is fixed in 9.2.0137. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                        │       │                   39d613cc06a86 
│                        │       ├ Title           : vim: Vim: Denial of Service via out-of-bounds write in
│                        │       │                   terminal handling 
│                        │       ├ Description     : Vim is an open source, command line text editor. Prior to
│                        │       │                   version 9.2.0565, the update_snapshot() function in
│                        │       │                   src/terminal.c copies the visible terminal screen into the
│                        │       │                    scrollback buffer when a snapshot is taken. For each
│                        │       │                   screen cell it walks the cell's chars[] array with no
│                        │       │                   upper bound, stopping only when it encounters a NUL
│                        │       │                   terminator. When a cell legitimately fills all
│                        │       │                   VTERM_MAX_CHARS_PER_CELL (6) slots — a base character plus
│                        │       │                    five combining marks — the bundled libvterm returns the
│                        │       │                   array without a terminating NUL, so the loop reads past
│                        │       │                   the fixed six-element array and appends the out-of-bounds
│                        │       │                   values to a buffer reserved for only six characters. A
│                        │       │                   program whose output is rendered inside a :terminal window
│                        │       │                    can trigger this with a short byte sequence and no Vim
│                        │       │                   scripting, leading to a crash. This issue has been patched
│                        │       │                    in version 9.2.0565. 
│                        │       ├ Severity        : LOW

│                                ├ Title           : zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer
│                                │                   overflow vul ... 
│                                ├ Description     : zlib versions 1.3.1.2 through 1.3.2 contain a heap buffer
│                                │                   overflow vulnerability in the gz_vacate() function when
│                                │                   processing non-blocking gzwrite() operations with stale
│                                │                   external buffer pointers. Attackers can trigger the
│                                │                   overflow by calling gzprintf() or gzvprintf() after a
│                                │                   write stall, causing an unchecked memmove() to write
│                                │                   beyond the internal input buffer boundary.

│                        │      ├ Title           : basic-ftp: basic-ftp: Denial of Service via crafted Unix
│                        │      │                   directory listings 
│                        │      ├ Description     : basic-ftp is an FTP client for Node.js. Prior to 6.2.1,
│                        │      │                   Client.list() can be forced by a malicious or compromised
│                        │      │                   FTP server to spend quadratic CPU time parsing a directory
│                        │      │                   listing because the RE_LINE expression in
│                        │      │                   src/parseListUnix.ts backtracks across adjacent
│                        │      │                   variable-length owner and group fields when a long
│                        │      │                   Unix-style line has a valid prefix but cannot satisfy the
│                        │      │                   later size and date fields. parseList() selects a parser
│                        │      │                   from the last nonblank line and then applies it to every
│                        │      │                   line, so a normal final line can select the Unix parser
│                        │      │                   while an earlier crafted line blocks the Node.js event loop
│                        │      │                    and freezes the process. This issue is fixed in version
│                        │      │                   6.2.1.

│                        │      │                   8223f735099b 
│                        │      ├ Title           : body-parser: body-parser: Denial of Service via unhandled
│                        │      │                   decompression stream error 
│                        │      ├ Description     : body-parser is body parsing middleware for Node.js and
│                        │      │                   Express. In versions before 1.20.9 and in versions from
│                        │      │                   2.0.0 before 2.4.0, a single request can crash any
│                        │      │                   application using body-parser with default options. When a
│                        │      │                   request carries a Content-Encoding such as gzip,
│                        │      │                   body-parser pipes it into a decompression stream and, after
│                        │      │                    reading the body, leaves that stream with no error
│                        │      │                   listener. A payload of one valid compressed frame followed
│                        │      │                   by trailing bytes decodes and the application responds
│                        │      │                   normally, but the trailing bytes then reach the
│                        │      │                   already-finished decoder, which emits an error that is
│                        │      │                   re-thrown as an uncaught exception and terminates the
│                        │      │                   process. No matching route is required because body parsing
│                        │      │                    runs before routing, so any endpoint that parses a body is
│                        │      │                    affected. The issue is fixed in body-parser 2.4.0 and
│                        │      │                   1.20.9, and users should upgrade to one of those versions
│                        │      │                   or later. As a workaround, disable request-body inflation
│                        │      │                   (set the body-parser inflate option to false) so encoded
│                        │      │                   requests are rejected before any decompression stream is
│                        │      │                   created.

│                        │      ├ Title           : follow-redirects: follow-redirects: Information disclosure
│                        │      │                   via improper regular expression escaping in sensitive
│                        │      │                   header filtering 
│                        │      ├ Description     : follow-redirects is a Node.js HTTP and HTTPS client wrapper
│                        │      │                    that automatically follows redirects. From 1.16.0 until
│                        │      │                   1.16.1, escapeRegex leaves valid header-name metacharacters
│                        │      │                    unescaped in sensitiveHeaders. When an application
│                        │      │                   declares a sensitive header whose name contains ^ or | and
│                        │      │                   follows a cross-origin or HTTPS-to-HTTP redirect, unescaped
│                        │      │                    regular-expression metacharacters prevent the generated
│                        │      │                   filter from matching the declared header name, and the
│                        │      │                   credential header is forwarded to an attacker-controlled
│                        │      │                   redirect target. This issue is fixed in version 1.16.1.

│                        │      ├ Title           : follow-redirects: follow-redirects: Information disclosure
│                        │      │                   via array-formatted headers during cross-origin redirects[
│                        │      │                   m 
│                        │      ├ Description     : follow-redirects is a Node.js HTTP and HTTPS client wrapper
│                        │      │                    that automatically follows redirects. From version 1.16.0
│                        │      │                   to before version 1.16.1, follow-redirects removes
│                        │      │                   sensitive credential headers (Authorization,
│                        │      │                   Proxy-Authorization, Cookie, and any caller-declared
│                        │      │                   sensitiveHeaders) before following a redirect that crosses
│                        │      │                   to a different host or downgrades to a less secure
│                        │      │                   protocol. The removal routine iterates the caller's headers
│                        │      │                    container with for...in and matches header names against a
│                        │      │                    filter. This assumes the headers container is a plain
│                        │      │                   object keyed by header names. Node's underlying
│                        │      │                   http.request, which follow-redirects is a drop-in
│                        │      │                   replacement for, also accepts headers as an alternating
│                        │      │                   array of names and values. For an array, for...in yields
│                        │      │                   the numeric indices "0", "1", "2" and so on, which never
│                        │      │                   match a header-name filter, so nothing is removed. An
│                        │      │                   application that sends array-form headers and follows an
│                        │      │                   attacker-controlled cross-origin redirect therefore
│                        │      │                   forwards its Authorization, Cookie, and Proxy-Authorization
│                        │      │                    headers verbatim to the attacker-controlled destination,
│                        │      │                   with no error or warning. The sensitiveHeaders option added
│                        │      │                    to fix CVE-2026-40895 / GHSA-r4q5-vmmm-2653 is equally
│                        │      │                   ineffective, because it relies on the same helper. This is
│                        │      │                   an unauthenticated confidentiality vulnerability: any
│                        │      │                   remote server the victim application contacts can harvest
│                        │      │                   the victim's credential headers by responding with a
│                        │      │                   cross-origin redirect. This issue has been patched in
│                        │      │                   version 1.16.1.

│                        │      ├ Title           : katex: katex: Cross-site scripting via prototype pollution
│                        │      │                   inheritance 
│                        │      ├ Description     : KaTeX is a fast, easy-to-use JavaScript library for TeX
│                        │      │                   math rendering on the web. From 0.11.0 until 0.18.2, KaTeX
│                        │      │                   uses ordinary JavaScript property access for the renderer
│                        │      │                   options object, the trust setting, default and processor
│                        │      │                   setting metadata, and namespace lookup and group
│                        │      │                   restoration, allowing inherited properties to be treated as
│                        │      │                    explicitly supplied values. When Object.prototype is
│                        │      │                   already polluted or an attacker controls the options
│                        │      │                   object's prototype, attacker-controlled mathematical
│                        │      │                   expressions can use an inherited trust value to enable
│                        │      │                   trusted rendering and produce links capable of
│                        │      │                   user-interaction cross-site scripting or loading
│                        │      │                   attacker-selected external resources in a consuming
│                        │      │                   application that inserts unsanitized KaTeX output into a
│                        │      │                   page. KaTeX does not itself create the prototype pollution,
│                        │      │                    and rendering an expression alone does not execute script.
│                        │      │                    This issue is fixed in version 0.18.2.

│                        │      │                   3ae2a98c8d92 
│                        │      ├ Title           : qs: qs: Denial of Service via unhandled exception during
│                        │      │                   array serialization 
│                        │      ├ Description     : ### Summary
│                        │      │                   
│                        │      │                   `qs.stringify` with `arrayFormat: 'comma'` throws
│                        │      │                   `TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value` when
│                        │      │                   an array element cannot be coerced to a string, such as an
│                        │      │                   object with an own non-callable `toString` (`{ "toString":
│                        │      │                   "x" }`) or a null-prototype object. The comma format joins
│                        │      │                   array elements with `Array.prototype.join` and, under
│                        │      │                   `encodeValuesOnly`, first passes each element through
│                        │      │                   `String()` in `utils.encode`; neither guards against an
│                        │      │                   element whose string coercion fails.
│                        │      │                   ### Details
│                        │      │                   In `lib/stringify.js`, the comma branch collapses the array
│                        │      │                    with `obj.join(',')`. For an element whose own `toString`
│                        │      │                   is not callable, `ToPrimitive` skips it, falls through to
│                        │      │                   `Object.prototype.valueOf` (which returns the object
│                        │      │                   itself), and throws. Under `encodeValuesOnly: true`, the
│                        │      │                   same element first reaches `String(str)` in `utils.encode`
│                        │      │                   (`lib/utils.js`) and throws there. Nested arrays (`{ "a":
│                        │      │                   [[{ "toString": "x" }]] }`) throw the same way, through
│                        │      │                   `Array.prototype.toString`. The `indices`, `brackets`, and
│                        │      │                   `repeat` formats walk into object elements instead of
│                        │      │                   coercing them, and are not affected.
│                        │      │                   Such elements can come from untrusted input. `JSON.parse`
│                        │      │                   produces `{ "a": [{ "toString": "x" }] }` with no qs option
│                        │      │                    involved. `qs.parse("a[0][toString]=x", { allowPrototypes:
│                        │      │                    true })` keeps the `toString` key, and
│                        │      │                   `qs.parse("a[][b]=c", { plainObjects: true })` produces a
│                        │      │                   null-prototype element; the default parse options drop
│                        │      │                   `toString` and produce ordinary objects, which do not
│                        │      │                   throw. Express 4's default `query parser`, Express 5's
│                        │      │                   `extended` query parser, and body-parser's `urlencoded({
│                        │      │                   extended: true })` all call `qs.parse` with
│                        │      │                   `allowPrototypes: true`.
│                        │      │                   #### PoC
│                        │      │                   ```js
│                        │      │                   var qs = require("qs");
│                        │      │                   qs.stringify(JSON.parse("{\"a\":[{\"toString\":\"x\"}]}"),
│                        │      │                   { arrayFormat: "comma" });
│                        │      │                   qs.stringify(qs.parse("a[0][toString]=x", {
│                        │      │                   allowPrototypes: true }), { arrayFormat: "comma" });
│                        │      │                   qs.stringify(qs.parse("a[][b]=c", { plainObjects: true }),
│                        │      │                   { arrayFormat: "comma", encodeValuesOnly: true });
│                        │      │                   // TypeError: Cannot convert object to primitive value
│                        │      │                   ```
│                        │      │                   #### Fix
│                        │      │                   Applied in a952e75 on `main` and released as v6.16.1: an
│                        │      │                   element whose string coercion would fail is coerced to its
│                        │      │                   primitive `valueOf`, if any, or else to
│                        │      │                   `Object.prototype.toString`, so it renders as `[object
│                        │      │                   Object]`, the same as any other object element already does
│                        │      │                    under the comma format. Nested arrays are walked the way
│                        │      │                   `join` walks them. Every input that did not previously
│                        │      │                   throw serializes exactly as before, and a `toString` or
│                        │      │                   `valueOf` that itself throws still propagates.
│                        │      │                   ### Affected versions
│                        │      │                   `>=6.7.0 <6.16.1`, fixed in v6.16.1.
│                        │      │                   The `join` path was introduced with the comma format in
│                        │      │                   b84acba and first shipped in v6.7.0; v6.6.x and earlier
│                        │      │                   ignore `arrayFormat: 'comma'` and are not affected. The
│                        │      │                   `encodeValuesOnly` `String()` site was introduced in
│                        │      │                   4c4b23d (v6.11.1); before that, the same input throws at
│                        │      │                   `join`. Every release from v6.7.0 through v6.16.0 is
│                        │      │                   affected.
│                        │      │                   ### Impact
│                        │      │                   An unauthenticated request can make any code path that
│                        │      │                   re-serializes attacker-influenced data with `qs.stringify`
│                        │      │                   and `arrayFormat: 'comma'` (for example, rebuilding a query
│                        │      │                    string from `req.query` for a redirect or an upstream
│                        │      │                   request, or serializing a parsed JSON body) throw
│                        │      │                   synchronously. In a typical Node.js HTTP framework the
│                        │      │                   throw is caught by the framework error boundary and the
│                        │      │                   affected request returns a 500; the process survives and
│                        │      │                   other requests are unaffected. Where the call runs outside
│                        │      │                   an error boundary, such as an `async` Express 4 handler
│                        │      │                   (where the throw becomes an unhandled promise rejection) or
│                        │      │                    a bare `http` request handler, the process exits, so the
│                        │      │                   impact in that case depends on the application error
│                        │      │                   handling rather than on qs. The default `arrayFormat`
│                        │      │                   (`indices`) is not affected.

│                        │      ├ Title           : shell-quote: shell-quote: Arbitrary command execution via
│                        │      │                   improper line terminator handling 
│                        │      ├ Description     : shell-quote's `quote()` function emits a `{ comment }`
│                        │      │                   token as `#` followed by its text, which comments out the
│                        │      │                   rest of the shell line, including the opening quote of any
│                        │      │                   later string token. A line terminator (\n, \r, U+2028,
│                        │      │                   U+2029) in that later string therefore ends the comment,
│                        │      │                   and the rest of the string is parsed as shell input:
│                        │      │                   `quote(['echo', 'ok', { comment: 'x' }, 'a\nid;#'])` runs
│                        │      │                   `id` in sh, bash, dash, ksh and zsh. `parse()` emits a
│                        │      │                   comment token for a `#` in the middle of a word (for
│                        │      │                   example `http://example.com/#frag`), so callers that
│                        │      │                   combine `parse()` output with another untrusted string,
│                        │      │                   such as
│                        │      │                   `quote(parse(untrustedCommand).concat(untrustedArg))`, are
│                        │      │                   affected. The fix for CVE-2026-9277 rejected line
│                        │      │                   terminators in the comment's own text, but not in the
│                        │      │                   tokens after it. Fixed in 1.11.0: `quote()` throws a
│                        │      │                   `TypeError` when a string after a `{ comment }` token
│                        │      │                   contains a line terminator. 
│                        │      ├ Severity        : CRITICAL

│                        │      │                   74d9216b0da6 
│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Certificate validation bypass via dropped
│                        │      │                   TLS options in Agent 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   4.0.0 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0
│                        │      │                   through 8.12.1, its Agent dispatcher passes its constructor
│                        │      │                    options through a JSON-based deep clone before forwarding
│                        │      │                   them to each per-origin pool, and because JSON cannot
│                        │      │                   represent functions, a caller-supplied tls option
│                        │      │                   containing a checkServerIdentity callback is silently
│                        │      │                   dropped before it reaches the TLS layer. As a result, a TLS
│                        │      │                    peer whose certificate a custom checkServerIdentity was
│                        │      │                   written to reject, but which passes Node's default hostname
│                        │      │                    and chain checks, is silently accepted. Because Agent is
│                        │      │                   the default dispatcher behind request, fetch, and
│                        │      │                   setGlobalDispatcher, this affects the path most
│                        │      │                   applications use, and EnvHttpProxyAgent is affected on its
│                        │      │                   direct and no-proxy routes as well, while only applications
│                        │      │                    that pass a function-valued tls option such as a custom
│                        │      │                   checkServerIdentity for certificate or public-key pinning
│                        │      │                   are at risk. The issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1,
│                        │      │                   and 8.12.2, which preserve the tls option outside the JSON
│                        │      │                   clone so custom verification callbacks are forwarded
│                        │      │                   unchanged, and users should upgrade to one of those
│                        │      │                   versions or later. As a workaround, pass the TLS options
│                        │      │                   through connect instead of tls, or for proxied destinations
│                        │      │                    use requestTls and proxyTls.

│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Cache poisoning and information disclosure
│                        │      │                   via improper cross-origin redirect caching 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   7.0.0 through 7.30.0 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, when an
│                        │      │                   originless Agent composes the redirect and cache
│                        │      │                   interceptors in that order with a shared cache store, the
│                        │      │                   cache builds its key from the original request URL before
│                        │      │                   the redirect handler changes the origin, so a response
│                        │      │                   produced after a cross-origin redirect is stored under the
│                        │      │                   original key. An attacker who controls the target of a
│                        │      │                   redirect from a trusted URL can have their response cached
│                        │      │                   under that trusted URL and served to later callers,
│                        │      │                   allowing persistent cache poisoning, and the same key
│                        │      │                   confusion lets a private, non-stored redirect response to a
│                        │      │                    user-specific resource be stored under the original URL
│                        │      │                   and served to a later unauthenticated caller, disclosing
│                        │      │                   private data. Applications are affected only when an
│                        │      │                   originless Agent, a shared cache store, and the
│                        │      │                   redirect-then-cache composition are all used. The issue is
│                        │      │                   fixed in undici 7.30.1 and 8.12.2, which verify the
│                        │      │                   producing origin still matches the cache key and preserve
│                        │      │                   each redirect hop's cache-control policy before storing,
│                        │      │                   and users should upgrade to one of those versions or later.
│                        │      │                    As a workaround, compose the cache interceptor before the
│                        │      │                   redirect interceptor, use per-origin dispatchers and cache
│                        │      │                   stores, or disable shared caching on redirect-capable
│                        │      │                   requests.

│                        │      │                   3fa5954369ee 
│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Denial of Service via unhandled stream
│                        │      │                   error on excessive content encodings 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   6.23.0 through 6.29.0, 7.18.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0
│                        │      │                   through 8.12.1, its fetch() implementation crashes the
│                        │      │                   Node.js process when a malicious server returns a response
│                        │      │                   with more than five content codings and closes the
│                        │      │                   connection before sending the body. undici rejects such
│                        │      │                   responses because of a content-encoding limit, but it
│                        │      │                   created the internal response stream before that check and
│                        │      │                   returned without attaching an error listener or aborting
│                        │      │                   the request, so the early close surfaces a content-length
│                        │      │                   mismatch on the orphaned stream, which Node.js treats as an
│                        │      │                    unhandled error and terminates the process. A remote,
│                        │      │                   unauthenticated server can trigger this with a single
│                        │      │                   response, even when the application correctly catches the
│                        │      │                   fetch() rejection, resulting in a denial of service. The
│                        │      │                   issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, and 8.12.2, and
│                        │      │                   users should upgrade to one of those versions or later.
│                        │      │                   There is no workaround.

│                        │      │                   1f1005e476c0 
│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Denial of Service via TLS renegotiation
│                        │      │                   with mismatched certificate 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   4.2.1 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0
│                        │      │                   through 8.12.1, the client process crashes when a TLS 1.2
│                        │      │                   server renegotiates after the connection is established and
│                        │      │                    presents a different, CA-trusted certificate whose
│                        │      │                   hostname does not match the requested host. Node.js re-runs
│                        │      │                    hostname verification on the renegotiated handshake and
│                        │      │                   destroys the socket with a certificate-altname error, but
│                        │      │                   undici's established-socket error handler asserted that
│                        │      │                   this error code could never occur, so the peer-controlled
│                        │      │                   error became an uncaught assertion that terminates the
│                        │      │                   Node.js process, affecting both the HTTP/1.1 and HTTP/2
│                        │      │                   paths. A malicious or compromised HTTPS endpoint reached
│                        │      │                   through undici or the global fetch() can crash the client
│                        │      │                   with a single server-initiated renegotiation, taking down
│                        │      │                   all in-flight requests and background work in the process,
│                        │      │                   and exploitation needs no CA compromise because the
│                        │      │                   attacker controls the endpoint and can present two ordinary
│                        │      │                    valid certificates. Only TLS 1.2 is affected, since TLS
│                        │      │                   1.3 does not support renegotiation. The issue is fixed in
│                        │      │                   undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, and 8.12.2, and users should upgrade
│                        │      │                    to one of those versions or later. As a workaround,
│                        │      │                   restrict outbound connections to TLS 1.3 so renegotiation
│                        │      │                   cannot occur, when the target endpoints support it.

│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Subresource Integrity bypass via
│                        │      │                   non-lowercase algorithm tokens 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   7.15.0 through 7.30.0 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, its fetch()
│                        │      │                    implementation verifies Subresource Integrity metadata by
│                        │      │                   matching the algorithm token against a lowercase-only set,
│                        │      │                   even though the SRI specification defines the token by its
│                        │      │                   ASCII-lowercase form, so a valid but non-lowercase token
│                        │      │                   such as an uppercase or mixed-case SHA256 is treated as
│                        │      │                   unknown and skipped. When no recognized algorithm remains,
│                        │      │                   undici treats the integrity list as empty and accepts the
│                        │      │                   response, so a server returning a body that does not match
│                        │      │                   the pinned digest passes the check. An attacker who
│                        │      │                   controls only the response body can therefore deliver
│                        │      │                   attacker-controlled bytes to an application that pinned a
│                        │      │                   valid uppercase or mixed-case SRI token, with no integrity
│                        │      │                   error, affecting response integrity only. The issue is
│                        │      │                   fixed in undici 7.30.1 and 8.12.2, which normalize the
│                        │      │                   algorithm token to ASCII lowercase before validation, and
│                        │      │                   users should upgrade to one of those versions or later. As
│                        │      │                   a workaround, use lowercase algorithm tokens such as
│                        │      │                   sha256, sha384, or sha512 in integrity metadata.

│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Denial of Service via memory exhaustion in
│                        │      │                   EventSource client 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   6.5.0 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0
│                        │      │                   through 8.12.1, its EventSource client can be driven to
│                        │      │                   exhaust process memory by a malicious or compromised
│                        │      │                   Server-Sent Events peer. By sending millions of tiny
│                        │      │                   completed data fields with no blank event separator, or a
│                        │      │                   single unfinished line split across many chunks, the parser
│                        │      │                    retains a growing amount of per-field and per-chunk state
│                        │      │                   that the byte-based maxEventSize and maxResponseSize limits
│                        │      │                    do not bound, and because maxResponseSize is enforced on
│                        │      │                   the compressed body before decompression, a small
│                        │      │                   compressed response can expand into enough retained memory
│                        │      │                   to terminate the process. An application only needs to
│                        │      │                   maintain an EventSource connection to an untrusted peer,
│                        │      │                   which controls only the response, and availability is the
│                        │      │                   only impact. The issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1,
│                        │      │                   and 8.12.2, which bound the retained parser state
│                        │      │                   independently of the byte limits, and users should upgrade
│                        │      │                   to one of those versions or later. There is no
│                        │      │                   workaround.

│                        │      │                   d07cc3aea9a2 
│                        │      ├ Title           : undici: undici: Denial of Service via unbounded WebSocket
│                        │      │                   PONG buffering 
│                        │      ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                        │      │                   5.15.0 through 6.29.0, 7.0.0 through 7.30.0, and 8.0.0
│                        │      │                   through 8.12.1, its WebSocket client, including the bundled
│                        │      │                    WebSocket exposed by Node.js, can be driven to exhaust
│                        │      │                   process memory by a malicious or compromised WebSocket
│                        │      │                   server. For every PING frame received, the client
│                        │      │                   automatically writes a PONG response and ignores the
│                        │      │                   backpressure signal from the socket write, so a server that
│                        │      │                    streams small PING frames while never reading the client's
│                        │      │                    PONGs makes the outbound write queue and heap grow without
│                        │      │                    bound until the Node.js process runs out of memory and
│                        │      │                   terminates. The attack is remote and unauthenticated, needs
│                        │      │                    only a normal WebSocket connection, and is asymmetric,
│                        │      │                   since small inbound PINGs produce a much larger retained
│                        │      │                   outbound queue, with availability the only impact. The
│                        │      │                   issue is fixed in undici 6.29.1, 7.30.1, and 8.12.2, which
│                        │      │                   pause WebSocket frame parsing when the automatic PONG
│                        │      │                   response hits socket backpressure and resume on drain,
│                        │      │                   bounding the outbound queue, and users should upgrade to
│                        │      │                   one of those versions or later. There is no workaround. 
│                        │      ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                               ├ Title           : undici: undici: Denial of Service via unhandled exception
│                               │                   in decompress interceptor 
│                               ├ Description     : undici is an HTTP client library for Node.js. In versions
│                               │                   7.15.0 through 7.30.0 and 8.0.0 through 8.12.1, its
│                               │                   decompress interceptor forwards decompressed response data
│                               │                   to the downstream handler from zlib stream event callbacks
│                               │                   without catching exceptions those callbacks may throw, and
│                               │                   while undici's engine converts a synchronous throw from a
│                               │                   downstream handler into a per-request failure, that
│                               │                   protection is absent when the throw happens asynchronously
│                               │                   from a zlib callback. As a result, a downstream handler
│                               │                   that throws by design, such as the built-in dump
│                               │                   interceptor which throws when a response exceeds its
│                               │                   configured maximum size, escapes as an uncaught exception
│                               │                   that terminates the Node.js process. A malicious or
│                               │                   compromised HTTP server can crash any client that composes
│                               │                   the decompress interceptor with such a handler by returning
│                               │                    a small compressed body that decompresses to more than the
│                               │                    configured limit, so only the decompressed size matters
│                               │                   and the bytes on the wire stay tiny. The issue is fixed in
│                               │                   undici 7.30.1 and 8.12.2, and users should upgrade to one
│                               │                   of those versions or later. As a workaround, avoid
│                               │                   composing the decompress interceptor with a response
│                               │                   handler that throws during response processing until
│                               │                   upgrading. 
│                               ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │      ├ Title           : golang.org/x/net/idna: golang: net/http:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/idna: Privilege escalation via incorrect
│                        │      │                   Punycode label processing 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The ToASCII and ToUnicode functions incorrectly accept
│                        │      │                   Punycode-encoded labels that decode to an ASCII-only label.
│                        │      │                    For example, ToUnicode("xn--example-.com") incorrectly
│                        │      │                   returns the name "example.com" rather than an error. This
│                        │      │                   behavior can lead to privilege escalation in programs using
│                        │      │                    the idna package. For example, a program which performs
│                        │      │                   privilege checks on the ASCII hostname may reject
│                        │      │                   "example.com" but permit "xn--example-.com". If that
│                        │      │                   program subsequently converts the ASCII hostname to
│                        │      │                   Unicode, it will inadvertently permits access to the
│                        │      │                   Unicode name "example.com".

│                        │      │                   4499d5e3e6b7 
│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: net/http: Denial
│                        │      │                   of Service via HTTP/2 trailer header memory exhaustion 
│                        │      ├ Description     : When "Trailer" headers are sent by a client, the HTTP
│                        │      │                   server internally uses the header values to populate the
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer map passed to the server handler. Because
│                        │      │                   Request.Trailer is a map, each entry incurs memory
│                        │      │                   overhead. For HTTP/2 servers, a malicious client can
│                        │      │                   exploit this by sending a "Trailer" header that declares a
│                        │      │                   large number of fields, causing the server to allocate a
│                        │      │                   disproportionate amount of memory while bypassing
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderValueCount and Server.MaxHeaderBytes
│                        │      │                   limits. This exploit is not applicable for HTTP/1 servers,
│                        │      │                   which do not support multiplexing a large number of
│                        │      │                   requests over one TCP connection, and whose
│                        │      │                   Server.MaxHeaderBytes are calculated differently. 
│                        │      ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: golang: golang.org/x/net/http2: net/http: HTTP
│                        │      │                   response smuggling via malformed HTTP/2 framing headers 
│                        │      ├ Description     : Historically, we have been rather lax about malformed
│                        │      │                   framing-related headers in our HTTP/2 implementation, as
│                        │      │                   they cannot interfere with HTTP/2 framing. However, this
│                        │      │                   makes it possible for our HTTP/2 implementation to forward
│                        │      │                   responses containing such headers to an HTTP/1 client when
│                        │      │                   acting as a reverse proxy. If the HTTP/1 client also does
│                        │      │                   not behave strictly enough, this can result in response
│                        │      │                   smuggling. 
│                        │      ├ Severity        : MEDIUM

│                        │      ├ Title           : net/http: net/http/internal/http2: golang:
│                        │      │                   golang.org/x/net/http2: golang: flow control limit bypass
│                        │      │                   via double refund in HTTP/2 server 
│                        │      ├ Description     : The HTTP/2 server can refund connection-level flow control
│                        │      │                   twice for the same data: Once when a client resets a stream
│                        │      │                    (refunding data for any sent-but-unread portion of the
│                        │      │                   stream), and again when a request handler reads the
│                        │      │                   buffered data. A malicious client can exploit this to
│                        │      │                   bypass the configured connection-level flow control limit
│                        │      │                   (MaxReceiveBufferPerConnection). Total buffered data is
│                        │      │                   still limited by the concurrent stream limit and
│                        │      │                   stream-level flow control. 
│                        │      ├ Severity        : MEDIUM
